## Natural history notes

A tiny free-floating aquatic plant characterized by oval to narrowly egg-shaped green fronds, typically only a few millimeters wide, with several fine roots hanging beneath each frond. Dotted Duckweed occurs in still or slow-moving freshwater habitats such as ponds, canals, lakes, sloughs, irrigation ditches, and wetlands, where it can reproduce rapidly and form dense mats across the water surface. In Florida, it is a widespread non-native species, likely introduced through the aquarium or aquatic-plant trade, and is classified as a Category 2 invasive by the Florida Invasive Species Council. Dense growth can reduce light penetration and dissolved oxygen beneath floating mats, potentially altering aquatic habitat conditions.
